messages:
jamie: Quick question — can we lock down who is allowed to flip the hotpath kill switch (hotpath-service.enabled) in prod? We had a near-miss this morning and the runbook is vague.

rui: Only oncall and SRE leads should actually press it. but we need explicit names and a CLI snippet. also: prefer scoped disable (region/canary) vs global off.

ana: fyi the recommended flow is: 1) confirm with oncall lead, 2) flip scoped in UI or via redwoodctl, 3) notify infra-alerts channel, 4) validate traffic shift and logs. we should add telemetry checkpoint.

sam: If it's latency or OOM spike, do a regional scoped flip first: set audience to 0% or route to fallback model. Only escalate to global if region-level doesn't help.

maria: Adding concrete commands here so people don't improvise: ```
# scoped disable (preferred)
redwoodctl flags set hotpath-service.enabled=false --scope=region:us-west-2 --audit-note=\"latency spike\" --actor=@jamie

# global emergency cut (SRE lead + oncall only)
redwoodctl flags set hotpath-service.enabled=false --scope=global --force --audit-note=\"emergency cut\" --actor=@<sre-lead>
```

rui: +1 to commands. also the CLI adds an audit entry but we need to confirm where the canonical audit is stored: logs --> https://telemetry.redwood.internal/flags/hotpath (must be searchable by thread id).

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2024-4512 (hotpath latency) by jamie. Audit token: a9f3-... Logs: s3://telemetry-prod/flags/hotpath/1745067890/

jamie: Good — two follow-ups: (1) who are the exact people authorized to flip global? list below and I will add to runbook. (2) can we enforce a two-person approval for global via the CLI/UI?

rui: Authorized global flippers: @rui (SRE lead), @ana (Head runtime), @sam (oncall manager). If none available, escalation goes to ENG oncall rotation + pagerduty escalation (must get verbal confirmation).

ana: On two-person approval — we can gate global with a quick approval flow in redwoodctl: ```
redwoodctl flags set hotpath-service.enabled=false --scope=global --require-approvals=2
``` that will post to /approvals and block until second ack. ops team will enable this by EOD.

sam: Add telemetry checklist to runbook: before flip: confirm error-rate>5% or p95 latency > 2s; after flip: confirm 95% traffic routed to fallback within 30s, monitor errors for 10m. Postmortem: attach flag audit id and graphs.

maria: Also include the quick verification commands: ```
# check active rollout
redwoodctl flags status hotpath-service --scope=region:us-west-2

# check routing table
redwoodctl routes get hotpath-service | grep fallback

# fetch audit entry
redwoodctl audit get --id a9f3-1745067890
```

jamie: Perfect. I'll update the runbook (runtime/runbooks/hotpath-kill.md) and add the list of names. Also adding a note: _do NOT_ rely on a single slack ack as approval — use the CLI approval flow or a recorded PD call.

rui: One more guardrail: automatic fallback after 5m if error rate doesn't drop should be disabled for global cuts (we don't want flapping). We'll put a manual cooldown requirement.

ana: I'll draft a one-page runbook change and ping legal/security for audit retention policy (we need 7 years for some customers).

jamie: Thanks everyone. tagging @ops-bot to pin this thread to the runbook once I push PR. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Pinned thread to runtime/runbooks/hotpath-kill.md and linked audit a9f3-1745067890."
